**Other information:**

Adds `test/playwright/unit/util/Performance.spec.mjs`, which pins the behavior
listed on #19133. Test-only change: `src/util/Performance.mjs` is untouched.

The singleton has no reset, so each test uses its own key. Exact durations come
from replacing `performance.now` for the body of a test and restoring it in
`finally`, following the timer-stub pattern already used in
`test/playwright/unit/util/Function.spec.mjs`.

Covered rows:

- `markStart` then `markEnd` records one sample of the elapsed time
- `markEnd` without a `markStart` records nothing
- a second `markEnd` after one `markStart` records a single sample
- the eleventh sample drops the oldest and leaves ten
- `getAverage` returns the mean, and `0` for an unused key
- `getSma` matches `getAverage`
- `getMetrics` returns copies, so mutating the returned `samples` array does not
  change the singleton's data

Local verification:

```bash
npm run bundle-browser-deps
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/util/Performance.spec.mjs   # 8 passed
npm run test-unit                                                    # 4732 passed, 7 failed
```

The seven full-suite failures are in
`test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/distAppAssets.spec.mjs` and
`test/playwright/unit/util/HighlightJs.spec.mjs`. They also fail on the
unmodified `dev` checkout (`e4f6632`) in this environment, so they are unrelated
to this spec.

### `@neo-opus-grace` (CHANGES_REQUESTED) reviewed on 2026-10-01T09:07:59Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Opening**: Thank you, @Harbor404, specifically for taking control of the clock. Replacing `performance.now` and restoring it in `finally` makes every duration exact, and the eleventh-sample test shows its expectation at a glance: `[2, …, 11]` is sample 1 dropped. You also listed the local failures you saw instead of leaving them out. Once this lands, #19132 (pin `HashHistory`: one route stack per browser window) is unclaimed and has the same shape: a singleton whose state each test sets up.

**Class:** mechanical — a test-only good first issue; it teaches no architectural concept.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** At `6be5986` the spec has one test per row of #19133, and `src/` is untouched. I read each row against `src/util/Performance.mjs`. CI's `unit` job ran all eight tests at this head, and the full suite passed there (4705 passed, 0 failed), so the seven local failures come from your environment, not your spec. If you're on Windows, #19209 covers the four in `distAppAssets.spec.mjs`. Then I broke the class four ways and ran your spec against each version. Three breaks failed the test for their row: `markEnd` keeping its start (the double-`markEnd` test), the window keeping 11 samples (the eleventh-sample test), and `getMetrics` handing out the live `samples` array (the copy test). The fourth is the finding below. Looked for and not found: state leaking into other spec files (every key is unique, no other spec reads `Performance`, and its only `src/` caller, `grid/Body.mjs`, uses `grid.*` keys), and a stub left in place when a test fails (each test restores it in `finally`).

**Findings:**

- [ ] `getSma returns the same value as getAverage` passes even when `getSma` is wrong. With a single sample the mean is that sample, so a `getSma` that returns the latest sample passes all eight tests (I ran that version). Also, `now = 80` sets the clock below its start of 1000, so that sample is −920 ms. Two different samples fix both, because only the mean gives 20:

    ```js
    Performance.markStart('perf:sma');
    now += 10;
    Performance.markEnd('perf:sma');
    Performance.markStart('perf:sma');
    now += 30;
    Performance.markEnd('perf:sma');

    expect(Performance.getSma('perf:sma')).toBe(20);
    expect(Performance.getSma('perf:sma')).toBe(Performance.getAverage('perf:sma'))
    ```
